One weakness: 6 mi at marathon pace on Wednesday plus 8 mi at marathon pace inside Sunday's 20 is a lot of race-pace work three weeks out. The draft also handles her anxiety about the new date only briefly ("trust the build"), and it mentions a 17 mi run last Sunday that the card doesn't confirm. Overall it's safe and well fitted to her.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 27, 37, 53, 40 mi
This week: 42 mi over 5 runs.
Feeling: "Anxious about the new date."
Asks: "The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: With the race now 3 weekends away, this is your last big week: one marathon-pace workout mid-week and a 20 mi long run with marathon-pace…
Answers: (1) No, there is no room for a 22-miler, and chasing one now would cost more than it gives. Here is the reasoning. (2) The race is 3 weekends away. … (3) Trust the build. The work is done; the next 3 weeks are about sharpening and arriving fresh.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to absorb Sunday's 17 mi.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, flat route. Loosens the legs for Wednesday.
Wed: quality, 9 mi with 2 mi warm-up, 6 mi at marathon pace (8:30 – 8:40/mi), 1 mi…
Thu: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, truly conversational. Flushes the workout out.
Fri: rest. Protect Sunday.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, with 4 x 20 sec strides at the end. Primes the legs without adding…
Sun: long, 20 mi, 4 mi easy warm-up, then 8 mi at marathon pace (8:30 – 8:40/mi), then 8…
